title: Frequency of Urination
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with urinary frequency, urgency, nocturia, weak stream, hesitancy, straining, and sensation of incomplete bladder emptying — classic LUTS (lower urinary tract symptoms) in an older man. DRE reveals enlarged, smooth, non-tender prostate. BPH is caused by benign proliferation of prostatic stromal and epithelial tissue, causing urethral compression. AUA symptom score quantifies severity. Labs: UA (rule out UTI), BMP (Cr — assess for obstructive nephropathy), PSA (age-appropriate screening). If mild: watchful waiting, lifestyle modifications. If moderate-severe: medical therapy — alpha-blockers (tamsulosin, alfuzosin — relax smooth muscle, rapid onset) ± 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (finasteride, dutasteride — shrink prostate, slow onset, reduce risk of urinary retention and surgery). Combination therapy for significant symptoms. Surgery (TURP) if refractory. Avoid anticholinergics and decongestants.
chief_complaint: Urinary frequency, urgency, nocturia, weak stream

stacks.label: Alpha-blocker (Tamsulosin)
stacks.finding: First-line. Rapid symptom relief. Relaxes prostatic smooth muscle.

stacks.label: 5-ARI (Finasteride / Dutasteride)
stacks.finding: If significant enlargement. Shrinks prostate, reduces retention risk.
